comparisons.finding: Best separation of record title, date and outcome. Detail heading and primary button remain readable at 200%. Ledger rows need a clearer opening affordance.

Disclosure arrows make expansion discoverable, but title, date and status share one long label. At 200%, wrapped summaries compete with the expanded claim; Record outcome lacks primary-button emphasis.
Claim and outcome button are clear, but the selector hides the history overview. The selected record title is visibly truncated at 200%, weakening identification.

Exact claim precedes clearly separated choices; optional original question stays secondary. Selected radio and Saved text provide visible confirmation. At 200%, Save requires scrolling but is shown reachable.

Compact choices initially fit well, but the claim being judged is hidden. Expanding the reference at 200% places a long claim and question before the choices, creating substantial reading and scrolling.
Persistent save area keeps confirmation visible, but the entry screen adds a Record outcome step. At 200%, the footer reduces the choice viewport; Not yet appears only after scrolling.

Explicit index links and section headings support continuous reading. Repeated Back to index links and long paragraphs create a lengthy 200% reading path; the index consumes much of the first viewport.

Strongest section overview: four clear disclosure rows with consistent separators. Expanded answers remain legible at 200%, and the end capture exposes subsequent sections without repeated navigation links.

Focused section reading is clean, including at 200%. Selector hides the section map, while generic Previous/Next labels omit destinations; Previous appears available on the first shown section without explaining its meaning.
Writing area initially resembles static prose; its boundary appears only on focus. Enlarged text ends mid-content without an obvious scroll cue. Focus outline and updated character count are visible.

Best field affordance and grouping: outlined input, adjacent count and full-width Done. Focus is conspicuous. At 200%, internal scrolling is necessary and text meets the field edge; Back's draft semantics remain unclear.

Outlined field and explicit Cancel/Done distinguish the commands well. Separate footer creates a large gap from the counter; enlarged text requires internal scrolling. Keyboard-visible behavior is not shown.

Strongest comparison: all three prices and supporting terms are exposed. Checkmark and matching simulation button identify selection. At 200%, the longer page retains readable prices, terms and a reachable action.

Selected offer and action are neatly grouped, with clear weekly-to-yearly changes. Selector hides competing prices and duplicates the selected price below, making comparison depend on remembering other offers.

Collapsed rows expose all headline prices, but initially none visibly identifies the weekly selection despite the weekly action. Expanded yearly content adds a clear Selected label while duplicating its price.
Destination summaries provide useful overview and spacious enlarged reading. Detail has a strong heading and Back control. Initial destination rows resemble static sections more than navigation.
Selector is recognizable, but hides the task overview. People appear as one dense paragraph mixing names, handles, signs and permissions; this becomes especially laborious at 200%.
Strongest navigation affordances: explicit disclosure arrows retain the section map around the shared forecast. At 200%, content wraps cleanly and the end capture shows Activity and Circle controls.

reason: Visible comparisons favor exposed information for history and pricing, the exact claim before check-in choices, disclosures for reference sections, and an unmistakable editor field. Scores are provisional judgments of the supplied composition and states. No variant demonstrates the complete evidence required for loop acceptance.
limitations: Reviewed attached sheets only; no source, other reviews, earlier rounds or live interaction inspected.
Feedback scores assess visible selection, counters and confirmation only. Null means feedback/recovery was not established; screenshot changes do not prove successful operations.

Accessibility scores address visible enlargement, wrapping, focus styling and affordances. Target dimensions, contrast ratios, keyboard navigation, focus restoration and assistive technology were not independently verified.
Component strengths and defects are included in each finding; scene scores do not certify every component individually.
Reported width coverage and absence of page errors or horizontal overflow were supplied context, not independently checked.
Storage, billing, social transport, error recovery, reduced motion, performance and physical/native behavior remain unverified. No full/native 9/10 certification or functional-success claim is made.
